Procedural Hit Reactions v1.1
Documentation & Changelog

1. Overview

Procedural Hit Reactions enables any humanoid, creature, or prop to flinch and recoil dynamically without manual animation. A lightweight runtime layer reads hit direction and blends additive pose offsets onto your Animator, delivering realistic reactions with minimal overhead.

Full Documentation & Tutorials:
https://ironsami-studio.gitbook.io/proceduralhitreactions

Join our Discord:
https://discord.com/invite/MapKXwNeDz

2. Files

  • BodyPartReactor.cs – assigns bone, profile, and per-bone multipliers.
  • HitReactionController.cs – collects reactors and exposes React().
  • ReactionProfile.cs – defines timing, strength, blend behavior, hit acceptance, axis locks, follow-through.
  • HitReactionTrigger.cs – attach to any projectile or weapon to forward collisions.
  • FPSController.cs – simple shooter controller for testing.
  • Demo – example scenes, prefabs, and pre-made profiles.

3. Getting Started

  1. Add HitReactionController to the root GameObject with your Animator.
  2. Add an Override layer (weight=1) in your Animator Controller; no clips needed.
  3. For each bone you want to react (e.g., Chest, Head):
    • Add BodyPartReactor.
    • Add a Collider and Rigidbody (kinematic or not).
    • Under the Profile header, Create New Profile or assign an existing one.
  4. Drag each reactor into the reactors list on the HitReactionController.
  5. Optionally trigger hits manually: 
    hitReactionController.React("Chest", hitDir, hitPoint);

4. HitReactionTrigger Setup

To automatically route hits:

  • Add HitReactionTrigger to your projectile or weapon prefab.
  • Set reactLayers to ignore environment layers.
  • On collision, the trigger finds the correct BodyPartReactor and calls React().
// Example:
var rocket = Instantiate(rocketPrefab, muzzle.position, muzzle.rotation);
rocket.GetComponent().reactLayers = LayerMask.GetMask("Characters");

5. ReactionProfiles (Fully Updated)

All main reaction settings now live in ReactionProfile for maximum reuse.

CategoryPropertyDescription
TimingreactionDurationLength of hit effect (sec).
blendInSpeedSpeed from 0→1 weight.
blendOutSpeedSpeed from weight→0.
Blend CurveblendCurveShape of weight over time.
RotationuseRotationEnable rotation offsets.
rotationStrengthMax random swing per axis.
rotationModeRandomOnly, DirectionOnly, RandomAndDirection.
directionRotationMultiplierMix factor (0=random,1=direction).
TranslationuseTranslationEnable position offsets.
translationStrengthMax random movement per axis.
translationModeRandomOnly, DirectionOnly, RandomAndDirection.
directionTranslationMultiplierUnits along hit direction.
Hit BehaviouruseContactPointDirectionUse contact point vector.
useLocalHitDirectionConvert hit vector to bone’s local space.
autoInvertBackHitsFlip vector for back hits.
Blend BehaviouradditiveAdd offsets or replace pose.
blendResetModeHardReset or ScaledCarryOver.
carryOverScaleFraction to preserve on reset.
slowBlendFactorFactor on blendIn (0=off).
offsetsFromCurrentPoseUse current pose as baseline.
Hit AcceptancehitAcceptanceIgnoreWhileActive or RestartTimer.
Axis LocksrotationAxisMaskEnable/lock per axis (1=allow).
translationAxisMaskEnable/lock per axis.

6. BodyPartReactor Options

SectionAction
ProfileAssign or Create New Profile button generates a new asset.

Per-Bone MultipliersintensityMultiplier, durationMultiplier scale strength/duration.

7. FollowObjects (New)

Define a list of objects to follow this bone’s reaction. Each FollowObject has:

  • transform – reference to the object.
  • rotWeight – rotation follow strength (0–1).
  • posWeight – position follow strength (0–1).

8. Demo Scene

Tip: Open the Demo scene, press Play, use W A S D to move and left-click to shoot and observe reactions.

9. Extending & Best Practices

  • Create multiple profiles for varied hit types (light, heavy, explosive).
  • Chain FollowObjects logically (e.g., gear, hair).
  • Combine with animation events for coordinated effects.
